audit.whatIsWrong: Row 1 is marked Swain although whys[1] says 'Level 2 stays even before Swain's root-combo tools are online', and row 3 is Skill although whys[3] says 'Levels 4-5 favour you'.
audit.why: Nevermove and Vision of Empire arrive at 3, not 2, so level 2 is even; once Zaahen has all three basics he wins the 4-5 window. Packet and mirror both read Skill / Skill / Swain / Zaahen / Skill / Swain / Swain, which fits 54.18% over 873 games.
audit.corrected: Row 1 to Skill, row 3 to Zaahen, in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns on either side, and the level-6 spike describes Demonic Ascension without saying what makes it dangerous.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1, Vision of Empire 22s, Death's Hand 7s, and Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s that lasts indefinitely while he keeps draining champions — it is not a fixed-duration ultimate you can wait out mid-fight. Zaahen's Q and E are 10s at rank 1, W 14s, R 110s.
audit.corrected: Number Nevermove at 12s and Vision of Empire at 22s, and state that Demonic Ascension persists as long as he drains, so the answer is to disengage rather than out-brawl it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swain's slots are swapped throughout the content layer — Nevermove is written as (W) and Vision of Empire as (E), when Nevermove is E and Vision of Empire is W. Two real interactions are also missing: Nevermove roots on the wave's RETURN, not on the way out, and Vision of Empire grants Swain a Soul Fragment when it hits a champion, so eating the poke literally heals him. Zaahen's E is also called 'Golden Onslaught' rather than Aureate Rush.
audit.why: Riot's text for E: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' For W: 'Champions hit are revealed and also grant Swain a Soul Fragment.' The missing-interaction file flags needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated on Ravenous Flock, which permanently raises his max health — so Grievous Wounds timing, not armour, decides the extended trade.
audit.corrected: Fix the slot letters, state the return-wave root as the thing to keep moving through, and put Grievous Wounds before the level-6 all-in rather than as a generic item line.

edits.after: Demonic Ascension is 120s and lasts while he drains — never brawl in it.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Combo when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove: matchup-defining — 12s at rank 1, and it roots on the return, not the way out. - Vision of Empire 22s: getting hit feeds him a Soul Fragment. - Demonic Ascension 120s: never brawl inside it.

edits.after: Level 3 favours Swain — Nevermove (E) roots on the return and his W poke holds the range.

edits.before: Level 3 belongs to Swain: once he has Nevermove (W) and Vision of Empire (E) he can root you from range and chunk you before you close, so don't walk into his W snare. But by levels 4-5 you flip it — dodge the root and your Darkin Glaive (Q) plus Golden Onslaught (E) gap-close to burst him while his kit is on cooldown.
edits.after: Level 3 belongs to Swain: with Nevermove (E, 12s) and Vision of Empire (W, 22s) he roots you from 850 and chunks you before you close — and the root lands on the wave's return, not the way out, so keep moving after it passes. By 4-5 you flip it: dodge that return and The Darkin Glaive plus Aureate Rush burst him.

edits.before: Swain's 6 is scary — Demonic Ascension (R) gives him huge sustain and AoE drain in a fight, so a sloppy all-in feeds him healing. Land your engage cleanly with Q knock-up and Final Retribution (R) to kill him before his R drain out-sustains your damage, or he wins the extended trade.
edits.after: Swain's 6 is scary — Demonic Ascension (R, 120s) stays up indefinitely while he keeps draining champions, so a sloppy all-in just feeds him healing. Buy Grievous Wounds first, land the Glaive recast knock-up, and kill him inside your R rather than trading through the drain.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a skill check as both of you farm, but stay wary — Swain wants to hit a lane-defining Nevermove (W) the moment he has it.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a skill check as both of you farm, but stay wary — Swain wants a lane-defining Nevermove (E) the moment he has it at 3.

edits.after: Level 3 tips to Swain when Nevermove (E) and Vision of Empire (W) let him poke and root from range, but 4-5 swings back to you: sidestep the returning wave and The Darkin Glaive knock-up plus Aureate Rush burst him while his E is down 12s.

edits.after: From first item on Swain is favoured — Demonic Ascension (R) heals through your damage and lasts as long as he keeps draining, so refuse the long brawl, carry Grievous Wounds, burst him before his R, and step up when Nevermove (E) is down 12s.

notes: Second systematic slot swap in this slice (after Singed): the content layer had Nevermove as (W) and Vision of Empire as (E) throughout. Corrected everywhere I edited. Best mechanical find: Nevermove roots on the wave's return, not the outbound, which changes the dodge entirely — and Vision of Empire feeds Swain a Soul Fragment when it hits you, so eating the poke heals him. Left diff/diffRating alone: TRICKY 7.5 sits oddly against a 54.18% win rate, but Swain's carry threat justifies it and the mirror's HARD/7-10 correction was for his side of the page.
